exampleAnswers.title: Finding Confidence Intervals for Intercept Parameters

question.text:
Let $\widehat{\,y}=\widehat{\,\beta}_0+\widehat{\,\beta}_1x=2.8-3.3x$ be the regression line fitted using a sample $(x_1,y_1), \: \ldots, \: (x_{10},y_{10})$ of $n=10$ paired observations. Assuming that all conditions for the simple regression model are satisfied, $\overline{x}=2.7,$ the mean square error of the model is $3.6,$ and $S_{xx} = \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 = 82.5,$ find a $99\%$ confidence interval for the $y$-intercept of the regression line.

Hint: Use the fact that $P(T > 3.355) = 0.005,$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $8$ degrees of freedom. Also, the standard error for $\widehat{\,\beta}_0$ is given by \[ \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,] = \sqrt{ \textrm{MSE} \cdot \bigg( \dfrac{1}{n} + \dfrac{\overline{x}^2}{S_{xx}} \bigg) } \]
question.explanation:
We use the following notations:

  • $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ is the regression line that best fits the population, and

  • $\widehat{\,y}=\widehat{\,\beta}_0+\widehat{\,\beta}_1x$ is the estimate of the "true" regression line given by the data in our sample.

In this case, we have that

\[ \widehat{\,y}=\widehat{\,\beta}_0+\widehat{\,\beta}_1x=2.8-3.3x. \]

We are told that all assumptions for a simple regression model are held. So, given a value $\alpha$ between $0$ and $1,$ the corresponding $[100(1-\alpha)]\%$ confidence interval for the $y$-intercept $\beta_0$ of our model can be written as

\[ \underbrace{\widehat{\,\beta}_0}_{\:\: \textrm{point} \\ \textrm{estimate}} \: \pm \: \overbrace{t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,]}^{\textrm{margin of error}}. \]

Note the following:

  • $\!\widehat{\,\beta}_0$ is our point estimate for the intercept, computed using the data points from our sample.

  • $P(T > t_{n-2,\alpha/2}) = \dfrac{\alpha}{2},$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $n-2$ degrees of freedom.

  • $\textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,]$ is the standard error of $\widehat{\,\beta}_0,$ given by \[ \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,] = \sqrt{ \textrm{MSE}\cdot\left(\dfrac1n+\dfrac{\overline{x}^2}{S_{xx}}\right)} \] where we have:

    • $\textrm{MSE}$ is the mean squared error of the model: \[ \textrm{MSE} = \dfrac{1}{n-2}\sum\limits_{i=1}^n (y_i - \widehat{\,y}_i)^2 \] where $\widehat{\,y}_i$ is the estimate of $y_i$ given by our regression model.

    • $S_{xx}$ is the usual sum of squares formula: \[ \displaystyle S_{xx} = \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 \]

To construct the confidence interval, we proceed as follows:

  • Step 1. Find the point estimate. From the regression equation $\widehat{\,y}=2.8-3.3x,$ our point estimate is
    \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_0 = 2.8. \]

  • Step 2. Find the margin of error. Since we are interested in finding a $99\%$ confidence interval, we have \[ \alpha=1-0.99=0.01 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \dfrac{\alpha}{2}=0.005. \] We are given that $P(T > 3.355) = 0.005.$ As a result, \[ t_{n-2,\alpha/2} = t_{8,0.005} = 3.355. \] Now, we can compute the margin of error: \[ t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,] = 3.355 \cdot \sqrt{3.6 \cdot \bigg( \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{2.7^2}{82.5} \bigg)} \approx 2.8 \]

  • Step 3. Determine the limits of the confidence interval: \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_0 \: \pm \: t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,] = 2.8 \pm 2.8 \]

question.text:
Height ($x$) $67$ $70$ $73$ $76$
Shoe size ($y$) $8.5$ $9$ $11$ $13$

The table above shows the heights, in inches, and corresponding shoe sizes of four randomly selected men. The corresponding linear regression line fitted using this sample is $\widehat{\,y} = -26.6 + 0.5x.$ Assuming that all conditions for the simple regression model are satisfied, $\overline{x}=71.5,$ and $\textrm{MSE}=0.338,$ find a $90\%$ confidence interval for the $y$-intercept of the regression line.

Hint: Use the fact that $P(T > 2.920) = 0.05,$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $2$ degrees of freedom. Also, the standard error for the $y$-intecept is \[ \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,] = \sqrt{ \textrm{MSE} \cdot \bigg( \dfrac{1}{n} + \dfrac{\overline{x}^2}{S_{xx}} \bigg) }. \]
question.explanation:
We use the following notations:

  • $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ is the regression line that best fits the population, and

In this case, we have that

\[ \widehat{\,y}=\widehat{\,\beta}_0+\widehat{\,\beta}_1x=-26.6 + 0.5x. \]

We are told that all assumptions for a simple regression model are held. So, given a value $\alpha$ between $0$ and $1,$ the corresponding $[100(1-\alpha)]\%$ confidence interval for the slope $\beta_1$ of our model can be written as

\[ \beta_0 \: \pm \: \overbrace{t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,]}^{\textrm{margin of error}}. \]

Note the following:

  • $\!\widehat{\,\beta}_0$ is our point estimate for the intercept, computed using the data points from our sample.

  • $P(T > t_{n-2,\alpha/2}) = \dfrac{\alpha}{2},$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $n-2$ degrees of freedom.

  • $\textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,]$ is the standard error of $\widehat{\,\beta}_0,$ given by \[ \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,] = \sqrt{ \textrm{MSE}\cdot\left(\dfrac1n+\dfrac{\overline{x}^2}{S_{xx}}\right)} \] where we have:

    • $\textrm{MSE}$ is the mean squared error of the model: \[ \textrm{MSE} = \dfrac{1}{n-2}\sum\limits_{i=1}^n (y_i - \widehat{\,y}_i)^2 \] where $\widehat{\,y}_i$ is the estimate of $y_i$ given by our regression model.

    • $S_{xx}$ is the usual sum of squares formula: \[ \displaystyle S_{xx} = \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 \]

  • Step 1. Find the point estimate. From the regression equation $\widehat{\,y}=-26.6 + 0.5x,$ our point estimate is
    \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_0 = -26.6. \]

  • Step 2. Find the margin of error.

    • Since we are interested in finding a $90\%$ confidence interval, we have \[ \alpha=1-0.9=0.1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \dfrac{\alpha}{2}=0.05. \] We are given that $P(T > 2.920) = 0.05.$ As a result, \[ t_{n-2,\alpha/2} = t_{2,0.05} = 2.920. \]

    • Computing $S_{xx},$ we get \begin{align*} \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 &= (67-71.5)^2 + (70-71.5)^2 + (73-71.5)^2 + (76-71.5)^2 \\ &= 20.25 + 2.25 + 2.25 + 20.25 \\[5pt] &= 45. \end{align*}

    • Now, we can compute the margin of error: \[ t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,] = 2.920 \cdot \sqrt{0.338\cdot \bigg( \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{71.5^2}{45} \bigg)} \approx 18.1 \]

  • Step 3. Determine the limits of the confidence interval: \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_0 \: \pm \: t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,] = -26.6 \pm 18.1 \]

\[ \beta_0 \: \pm \: \overbrace{t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_0\,]}^{\textrm{margin of error}}. \]

    \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_0 = 151.3. \]
